extracted.intended_audience: NIH K01 applicants, mentors, institutional research administrators, and NIH peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Summary Statement / peer review critique for an NIH K01 Mentored Research Scientist Development Award (resubmission), documenting criterion-level evaluations, strengths/weaknesses, and administrative determinations. Intended to guide applicants and program staff about review outcomes and required follow-ups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Priority Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact: This application received an Overall Impact/Priority score of [numeric score].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The impact/priority score is calculated by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. The criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by the individual reviewers assigned to an application, and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score. Some applications also receive a percentile ranking. See http://grants.nih.gov/grants/peer_review_process.htm#scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the applicant's record and potential to develop into an independent investigator (productivity, prior training, relevant experience, publications, prior funding, letters of recommendation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate strengths and weaknesses such as dedication to research, publication record (first-author papers), prior relevant grants, leadership roles, and whether the applicant may be 'too advanced' for a K award. Statements include specific concrete evidence (e.g., number of publications, prior awards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Plan / Career Goals & Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the quality, feasibility, and appropriateness of the proposed career development activities, training goals, coursework, experiential training, timeline, and how they support transition to independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for clearly articulated training goals (here: 4 training goals), a realistic mix of didactic and experiential learning (courses, on-site training, validation experiments), mentoring interactions (frequency of meetings), participation in peer support activities (K club, grant writing workshops), and alignment between training activities and research aims. Overly ambitious course loads are noted as prior weaknesses; applicants should detail how prior concerns were addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the scientific aims, study design, preliminary data, feasibility, analytic approaches, sample size justification, and potential impact of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate clinical relevance, novelty, rationale for aims, integration with parent studies (e.g., CARPE DIEM), preliminary results (PLS-DA plots, radar plots), sample size (cases/controls), case definitions and gold standard limitations (e.g., NP swabs detect colonizing organisms), and missing methodological details (for example, whether CAP diagnosis requires X-ray). Weaknesses include small sub-cohorts (e.g., bacterial monomicrobial cases) and potential false positives in etiology assignments; reviewers may suggest enrichment strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor(s), Co-Mentor(s), Consultant(s), Collaborator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the mentoring team composition, expertise, roles and responsibilities, prior mentoring track records, and funding/stability of mentors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers expect clearly delineated mentor roles (tables of responsibilities), mentors with relevant expertise (metabolomics, biostatistics, clinical pediatrics), evidence of active engagement (frequency of meetings, mentorship committee), and consideration of mentors' funding status (concern if primary mentor's funding is near end date). Strengths include mentors' publication and mentoring records, and availability of hands-on training opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment and Institutional Commitment to the Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of institutional support, research infrastructure, available facilities, resources (e.g., NMR spectrometer, metabolomics labs), data management, and protected time for the candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note institutional investments (internal funding, server space, proximity to mentors), availability of cores and collaborations (e.g., University of Michigan metabolomics core), and whether the candidate's retention depends on the award. Strong institutional commitment and existing infrastructure are strengths; lack of institutional support would be a weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Code: 30 ACCEPTABLE. The application adequately addresses these four points: Risks to human subjects; Adequacy of protections against these risks; Potential benefits of the proposed research to human subjects; and Importance of the knowledge to be gained from this project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects involving human subjects must conform to NIH policies on protection of human subjects. Reviewers assess risk/benefit balance, protections and consent procedures, and overall justification. See PHS398 application materials and http://grants.nih.gov/grants/policy/hs/index.htm for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: DATA AND SAFETY MONITORING PLAN: ACCEPTABLE
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers determine whether a Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) is required. Comment example: 'Concur no need for DSMB. The PI will monitor for anticipated and unanticipated issues.' The PI should describe monitoring responsibilities and contingency plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: INCLUSION OF WOMEN PLAN (Resume): Code: G1A ACCEPTABLE
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow NIH policies on inclusion of women in study populations; provide rationale for inclusion/exclusion and expected demographics. Example given: anticipated ~48% female based on ED demographics. See http://grants.nih.gov/grants/funding/women_min/guidelines_amended_10_2001.htm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Minorities Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: INCLUSION OF MINORITIES PLAN (Resume): Code: M1A ACCEPTABLE
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow NIH policies on inclusion of minorities; include demographics and rationale. Example demographics provided (approx. 48% white, 45% black/African American, 96% non-Hispanic). Submit details to NIH program administrator prior to studies. See NIH inclusion policy guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Children Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: INCLUSION OF CHILDREN PLAN (Resume): Code: C2A ACCEPTABLE
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify age ranges and justify inclusion/exclusion. Example: 'Only children, 3 months to 11 years of age will be included.' Projects must conform to NIH policies on inclusion of children; provide details to NIH program administrator before undertaking the studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether vertebrate animals are used and provide appropriate animal care and use documentation when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazard Comment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If biohazards are present, applicants must describe containment and biosafety procedures; if none, state not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: RESUBMISSION: Comments: See above reviewer comments. All issues were addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For resubmissions, reviewers examine whether prior concerns were addressed and whether revisions sufficiently responded to the critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: TRAINING IN THE RESPONSIBLE CONDUCT OF RESEARCH: ACCEPTABLE
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate format, subject matter, faculty participation, duration, and frequency of RCR training. Example components: formal ethics course, seminars, CITI training, monthly faculty conferences, annual symposia, and specified hours over award period. Applications must include plans for RCR training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: RESOURCE SHARING PLANS: NOT APPLICABLE (Data Sharing Plan, Sharing Model Organisms, Genomic Data Sharing Comments if >$500,000/year)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable (e.g., large awards), applicants must include data sharing, model organism sharing, and genomic data sharing plans per NIH policy; reviewers may comment on adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: AUTHENTICATION OF KEY BIOLOGICAL AND/OR CHEMICAL RESOURCES: UNACCEPTABLE
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate 1 page 'Authentication' document using the new NIH Forms D should be uploaded with the application. See 'Implementing Rigor and Transparency in NIH & AHRQ Career Development Award Applications' http://grants.nih.gov/grants/guide/notice-files/NOT-OD-16-012.html. Addressing this requirement is mandatory; failure to include the document is judged unacceptable by reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: BUDGET AND PERIOD OF SUPPORT: The budget was recommended as requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The budget shown is the requested budget and has not been adjusted to reflect reviewer recommendations; if an award is planned, grants management staff will calculate costs based on committee recommendations. Include justification for personnel and project costs; reviewers may comment on adequacy of budget justification.
